findings.location: stanza urn:x-opensiddur:text:poem:hayom_teamtseinu/24: chapter milestones corresp=".../24/quotation/deuteronomy/6/for_verse_24" and ".../24/quotation/deuteronomy/6/for_verse_25"; verse milestones ".../24/quotation/deuteronomy/6/24" and ".../6/25"
findings.problem: The quote-context chapter URNs are not the parent path of their verse URNs. Each chapter URN has an extra synthetic segment (for_verse_NN) at the same depth as the verse, so .../deuteronomy/6/24 sits as a sibling of its own chapter's URN, not a child. The path .../24/quotation/deuteronomy/6 is never assigned. The two chapter milestones were clearly made different to avoid giving one identity twice (the intervening וְנֶאֱמַר / 'And it was said' cue is correctly kept outside), but the workaround breaks the hierarchy. I have not checked how refdb's UNIT_CONTAINED_BY or its component-count fallback (line 182) handles a chapter URN with as many components as a verse.
findings.guideline_evidence: JLPTEI-3.md:40 ('The remainder of the URN is hierarchical'); :220-223 (quote-context chapter and verse milestones keep canonical chapter/verse values); :182 (scope fallback counts '/'-separated components)
findings.required_change: Tell the two quotation contexts apart at a level above the book/chapter/verse path, so each verse URN is a child of its chapter URN. For example: .../24/quotation/1/deuteronomy/6 + .../24/quotation/1/deuteronomy/6/24, and .../24/quotation/2/deuteronomy/6 + .../24/quotation/2/deuteronomy/6/25, or whatever the project's established form is. Make the same change in both HE and EN so the parallel rows still pair up. Keep @n=6/24/25 unchanged.

findings.problem: This prayer-part milestone sits inside the shalom div, but its URN is a sibling of .../repetition/shalom, not a child. The name also describes the edition ('english_extra') rather than the text (the peace chatimah). Giving the documentary EN blessing its own identity, separate from the final one used by the expanded text, is correct (line 226-227). The problem is only where the URN sits and how it is named. Practical effect: resolving the URN places this part outside the shalom section even though the document contains it there, and the name ties a reusable text identity to one project's language. Whether to register it is the separate registry review and is not judged here.
findings.guideline_evidence: JLPTEI-3.md:40 (hierarchical URNs); :46-50 (a URN names a text that could have several project representations); :226-227 (do not duplicate a canonical URN merely because it is printed again)
findings.required_change: Move the identity under the enclosing division, e.g. .../repetition/shalom/<text-descriptive-name>, and name it after the text rather than the English edition. Keep it separate from the final chatimah's URN. Pass the new name to the separate registry review.

findings.location: shalom/proofs, quotation of deuteronomy/4/4: <tei:choice><tei:sic>this day.</tei:sic><tei:corr>this day’.</tei:corr></tei:choice> placed inside tei:seg and before the verse/chapter terminators
findings.problem: The corrected closing quotation mark (’) and the period fall inside the Deut 4:4 seg and inside the quote-context verse and chapter scopes. In the same paragraph, the opening ‘ and the Prov 9:11 closing-quote choice (‘. → ’.) are correctly kept outside the seg. The result: the corrected reading's verse scope includes English quotation punctuation, and the two quotations in one paragraph are bounded inconsistently. The words 'this day' are needlessly duplicated in sic and corr.
findings.guideline_evidence: JLPTEI-3.md:217-226 (the quotation seg and its contextual URNs identify only the bounded quoted extent; close inner scopes exactly at that extent); task brief: English linkage cues are excluded from prayer words
findings.required_change: Keep 'this day' as plain seg content. Close the verse, then the chapter, then the seg. After the seg, encode <tei:choice><tei:sic>.</tei:sic><tei:corr>’.</tei:corr></tei:choice>. This still preserves the printed punctuation error.

findings.location: stanza poem:hayom_teamtseinu/23, seg source=urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:isaiah/56/7: text ends '...for all peoples’. ' inside the seg, before the verse/chapter terminators
findings.problem: The closing English quotation mark is inside the Isa 56:7 seg and its verse scope. The opening ‘ is outside, and in the same file the Deut 6:24/6:25 closing ’. is correctly placed after the terminators. The bounded extent of Isa 56:7 therefore takes in a linkage cue, inconsistently with the neighbouring quotations. The cross-page tei:pb inside the seg is correct and should stay where it is.
findings.guideline_evidence: JLPTEI-3.md:217-226; task brief: English linkage cues are excluded from prayer words
findings.required_change: End the seg at 'for all peoples' (with or without the final period, matching the house style used for Deut 6:24/25) and move ’ outside, after the verse and chapter terminators. Leave the single bound quotation and the internal pb unchanged.

verified: Headers: every file's idno URN matches its div @corresp plus @project for that project; div @corresp carries no project (line 40). sourceDesc uses /{PROJECT}/index#project_source_bibl with no extension (lines 52-66).

Facsimile links follow /page/n(scan-1).jpg. Printed 146 HE → n311. 147 HE n313 / EN n314. 148 HE n315 / EN n316. 149 HE n317 / EN n318 (kehayom pb 149 HE n317, EN n318; kaddish_preface and full_kaddish divs HE n317 / EN n318). 150 (sequential scan 320) → n319 for ein_keloheinu and pittum_haqetoret. Each file's biblScope page numbers match its facsimile pages.

Hayom: stanzas run poem:hayom_teamtseinu/1-4, techaddesh, 21, teqabbel (musaf_hayom_teamtseinu); /22 (musaf_hayom_titmekhenu); /23 and /24 (musaf_kehayom_hazeh). Not numbered 1-7. Every Amen prayer-part milestone opens after the stanza terminator, so Amen is outside stanza scope. HE and EN use identical stanza and Amen URNs.

Stanza 22 (titmekhenu) is conditional, and that is backed by the printed instruction ויש מוסיפים. Its condition URN is condition:poem:hayom_teamtseinu/22/recite: it mirrors the text URN plus a variant name and has no project (lines 68-76).
Deut 6:25 is encoded unconditionally inside stanza 24 in both HE and EN. No optional control was invented for it.
Isa 56:7 is one seg in both languages with the tei:pb inside it. The quotation is not split at the page break. The verse and chapter terminators close before the stanza terminator.

Quote-context URNs are contextual (…/quotation/<book>/<ch>/<v>) with canonical @n. The canonical bible URN appears only as seg @source, never as a duplicated @corresp (lines 220-227). The partial quotations (Num 6:26 single words in kohanim_response_3_6/3_7; Isa 57:19 without בורא ניב שפתים) carry only contextual corresp URNs, so they do not present themselves as the canonical whole verse.

Inner quote-context milestones inside seg type=quotation (kohanim_ribbon Deut 26:15, sim_shalom proofs, kaddish_preface, full_kaddish/6 and /8) close both scopes before the seg ends. Milestones placed before the span (kohanim_response, kehayom) are closed right after it. The enclosing prayer-part or stanza milestone always stays outside the span.

Role labels (חזן, ק׳/קהל with abbr/expan) in HE full_kaddish are tei:note type=description with instruction:role corresp, placed before the prayer-part milestone, so they sit outside the word scopes. In yehi_ratzon, the instruction ויכוין לסיים… precedes the amen prayer-part milestone. Labels and instructions are notes, not prayer text, and carry no rend.

yehi_ratzon optional clauses (wife_and_children, parents) are well-formed: j:conditional type=marked with an xml:id, a matching j:endConditional @target, and condition URNs that mirror the text URN with no project.
EN sim_shalom Prov 9:11 sic/corr (‘. → ’.) preserves the printed punctuation error and sits outside the seg.

Partial-translation alignment: EN files exist only for parts the EN prints; the late Hebrew-only parts (ein_keloheinu, pittum_haqetoret on page 150) have no EN substitute; and corresponding HE/EN files use identical prayer-part, stanza, chapter and verse URNs.
Prayer-part, stanza, chapter and verse milestones all have explicit terminators. None depends on a paragraph or line closing tag (lines 209-215).

Biblical citations checked against the verse text: numbers/6/26, chronicles_1/29/11, isaiah/57/19, deuteronomy/26/15, proverbs/9/11, deuteronomy/4/4, isaiah/56/7, deuteronomy/6/24, deuteronomy/6/25, numbers/14/17, psalms/25/6, psalms/113/2, psalms/121/2 all match the quoted wording.
limitations: I read only the two permitted files. The JSON holds 22 files (20 distinct stems, HE+EN). 'all_group_files_read' means every entry in that JSON; I cannot independently confirm the JSON lists the whole group.

No scans were viewed. I cannot confirm whether the yehi_ratzon wife/children and parents clauses are visibly marked as optional in print, so type=marked is accepted as encoded, not verified. Likewise I cannot confirm whether the printed parentheses around (הַקָּב) in pittum_haqetoret mark a variant that needs a control; it is currently left as plain text, which avoids inventing a condition.
The EN counterparts for dream, kohanim_ribbon, yehi_ratzon and titmekhenu are not in this JSON. I cannot verify whether the EN prints them or whether they live in another group.

Not checked against the reference database or schema: whether the existing registry already holds IDs for ein_keloheinu/{ein,mi,nodeh,barukh,attah,incense}, hayom_teamtseinu/{techaddesh,teqabbel}, kohanim_response_3_6/3_7, or the shalom chatimah; whether prayer:qorbanot/pittum_haqetoret refers to exactly the printed extent; whether a tei:note is allowed directly inside j:conditional (as in musaf_hayom_titmekhenu); and how refdb treats the for_verse_NN chapter URNs.

Seg @type=quotation is present in some files (kohanim_ribbon, sim_shalom, kaddish files) and absent in others (kohanim_response, kehayom). Lines 217-219 do not require it, so this is not raised as a finding.

Source readings, pointing and transcription accuracy (e.g. ייָ vs יְיָ in HE Deut 4:4, unpointed titmekhenu) are outside this review's scope. Questions 473-489 remain open. Nothing here certifies the source or the overall batch.
